chunks: And from him, from al-Husayn, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And to Allah is due the pilgrimage of the House for whoever is able to find a way to it.' He said, 'He walks, if he does not have [a mount].' I said, 'He is unable to walk.' He said, 'He walks and rides.' I said, 'He is unable to do that.' He said, 'He serves the people and goes out with them.' This report is considered recommended (mustahabb) based on the indication of the preceding reports.
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is considered recommended (mustahabb) based on the indication of the preceding reports.
ai.seo_question: What are the graduated levels of physical and financial ability required for Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith elucidates the gradations of 'ability' (istita'ah) for Hajj by establishing a practical hierarchy: walking if one cannot afford a mount, and serving the caravan if one cannot walk. Shaykh al-Tusi notes in the chain that this specific narration is understood as indicating recommendation (istihbab) rather than strict obligation, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that the duty is fulfilled through proportional effort based on one's physical and financial capacity.
